Day trips

Aix-en-Provence

A city of art, water and light. Aix-en-Provence charms visitors with its Provençal elegance, its fountains and the legacy of Cézanne.

45 min by car from Cassis

Once the capital of Provence, Aix-en-Provence is a city to be savoured. The café terraces of the Cours Mirabeau, fountains murmuring on every street corner, 17th-century mansions and the light that inspired Cézanne. Allow a whole day to enjoy its markets, museums and shops.

Things to see

The must-sees

Art, heritage and the art of living — the essence of Provence.

Must-see

The Cours Mirabeau

Aix's most famous avenue, lined with century-old plane trees, historic cafés (Les Deux Garçons) and fountains. Take a stroll and enjoy a coffee on a terrace — the meeting place of the people of Aix since the 17th century.

Terraces, fountains and century-old plane trees

The old town and its fountains

Aix is nicknamed the ‘city of a thousand fountains’. Wander through the pedestrian streets and discover the grand mansions, Saint-Sauveur Cathedral and the shady squares. Every corner holds a surprise.

Allow 2 to 3 hours for a leisurely wander
Our favourite

Caumont Centre d'Art

A beautifully restored 18th-century mansion hosting internationally renowned temporary art exhibitions. Formal French gardens, a tearoom and an immersive film about Cézanne's Provence.

Current exhibitions

The Atelier Cézanne

The master's studio, preserved just as he left it. His objects, easels and the light that inspired his still lifes. In the hills above Aix, with a view of the Sainte-Victoire — the painter's obsessive motif.

Info & booking

The markets of Aix

Place Richelme — daily food market with local producers. Place des Prêcheurs — flower and craft market. On Tuesdays, Thursdays and Saturdays, the big market spreads across the whole old town.

Every day on Place Richelme — Big market: Tue, Thu, Sat
